brief: Natural toothpaste and deodorant, you know the stuff. Just show it to whoever. Cheap, like $5 or so.

profile.business_summary: A budget-friendly brand selling natural personal care essentials, specifically toothpaste and deodorant, priced around $5.

relevant_tags.why: The advertiser explicitly describes their products as natural toothpaste and deodorant.
Consumers looking for natural toothpaste and deodorant are highly likely to seek non-toxic alternatives.
Personal care products like deodorant and oral care fall under the broader beauty and personal care category.
Toothpaste and deodorant are daily personal care essentials typically kept in the bathroom.
A low-cost, everyday essential is highly convenience-oriented.

persona_conflicts.evidence: "Natural toothpaste and deodorant, you know the stuff. Just show it to whoever."
"Natural toothpaste and deodorant, you know the stuff."

note_signals.why: A cheap ($5) daily essential is highly impulse-friendly and fits Swiftcart's convenience/grocery basket profile.

profile.gate_reason: The product type (natural toothpaste and deodorant) and budget price point ($5) are clear enough to map to relevant personal care, wellness, and grocery publishers.

config.advertiser_summary: A budget-friendly brand selling natural personal care essentials, specifically toothpaste and deodorant, priced around $5.

assumptions: repeat_consumable: assumed 2.5 orders per customer over ~6 months.
No target CPA/ROAS or margin given; assumed 70% gross margin (typical for beauty). Give a target CPA to replace this.
Target CPA = 70% of max affordable CAC ($5 x 70% margin x 2.5 orders = $8.75).

pricing.rationale: Acquisition goal with no conversion history: pay per click. Max CPC = target CPA $6.12 x click-to-purchase rate (1.4%-4.9% for beauty). Clicks are observable without trusting a pixel, so both sides can verify billing.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.

budget.pacing: even daily pacing; pause a host if CPA > 2.0x target after 150 clicks

allocations.rationale: score 0.18 -> relative fit x1.40 on CTR/CVR; max bid $0.25 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.16 -> relative fit x1.32 on CTR/CVR; max bid $0.25 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.15 -> relative fit x1.26 on CTR/CVR; max bid $0.25 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.14 -> relative fit x1.23 on CTR/CVR; max bid $0.25 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.13 -> relative fit x1.16 on CTR/CVR; max bid $0.25 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%

warnings: No budget given: recommending $440, the smallest budget that buys 300 clicks per host.

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: bid = start bid per host (70% of break-even); pacing adjustment only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded by bid changes

phases.name: enhanced_cpc
phases.until: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.
phases.rule: bid = start bid x conversion_likelihood x pacing, clamped to [floor, max bid]
phases.why: spend more on shoppers who look likely to buy, never above break-even

phases.name: target_cpa
phases.rule: Disco bids automatically to hit $6.12 CPA
phases.why: only once Disco can predict this brand's conversion rate

adjustments.reason: Bid higher when the shopper looks like a high converter: their persona match for this campaign vs the host's average shopper (from the serve-time persona posterior).
Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.

bid_strategy.rationale: Start below break-even and fixed so the first two weeks measure the hosts, not the bidder; then bid per shopper within a hard ceiling (max CPC = target CPA x CVR), so a single click can never cost more than it's expected to earn.
